source.title: Understanding Positional Features in Layer 0 SAEs

record.file_problem: none; the full informal research note is present, though the referenced figures are not included as images.
record.tranche_reason: It measures SAE features and their positional geometry in a language model, providing a conceptual test of whether an SAE can recover sparse features; it is not a reproduction of the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The note reports its own measurements of gpt2-small layer 0 SAE features and their behavior beyond the training context. Claims or results attributed to other posts and papers are not recorded as this study's results. The referenced plots are not included, so rows use only outcomes stated in the text or figure caption.
record.test_reason: The note measures what a layer-0 SAE on gpt2-small recovers: about 50 positional features tiling a helical positional manifold, separate from semantic features. It also shows how those features fail beyond the SAE's training context. These are its own measurements bearing on V4, V5 and, through the manifold geometry, V6. It does not reproduce the toy-model method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors think the length-generalization failure may matter little for modern models with rotary embeddings, citing Pythia SAEs. They also suggest that fine-tuning the SAE on longer contexts may fix it.
record.recipe_differences: Measures features learned by a layer 0 SAE on gpt2-small rather than testing the original toy-model setup; focuses on positional embeddings and SAE length generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE context length: features trained with context_size=128 behave poorly beyond that context; early and later positions have different feature allocation.
record.problems: One model, one layer, and one SAE context size are studied. The note gives no uncertainty estimates or controls and does not report tests across SAE trainings. Some evidence is described through referenced plots whose images are not present in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results omitted. Cited findings about other SAEs or models, including the Pythia/rotary-embedding comparison, are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: No toy networks and no sparsity sweep.
Neuron polysemanticity and capacity competition are not studied.
Other causes of polysemanticity are not studied.
Only one model, layer 0, one SAE, and no spread across neurons. Later layers, where position and semantics mix, are not tested.
Stability across SAE seeds or widths is not measured. Width-scaling of the feature count is predicted but not tested.
No direct test of whether features are 1-D. The evidence is only the PCA and manifold-tiling observation for positional embeddings.

missing.what: Pre-ReLU positional feature activations are near-sinusoidal and cross zero once in context. Early-position features fire more strongly and are more numerous.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal note without controls or uncertainty estimates, and its figures are absent from the text. The reconstruction-error blow-up beyond the context length is cited from other posts, not measured here. The V6 link is my reading of the geometry result, not the authors' framing, although they compare it to Engels et al.'s circular features.

versions.untested_parts: No small toy networks or controlled sweep over feature count, sparsity, or dimensions.
Does not test polysemantic neurons or whether feature importance and limited neuron capacity cause them; its observations concern positional SAE features.
Does not test other causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE recovery of positional and semantic features in one model and layer; does not test feature spread across neurons, other models, or later layers.
Does not test stability across SAE trainings or models, or establish whether SAE features are canonical units generally.
Does not test whether the underlying superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Counted features by their mean activation across tokens at each position, using the maximum over positions as a positional score.
rows.note: The note describes these as features learned by the SAE.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected positional feature activations across positions within the SAE training context.
rows.measure: Position coverage and allocation across positional SAE features
rows.value: All positions get some positional features; features generally span a range of positions, later positions share features across several positions, and the first few positions get dedicated (sometimes several) features.
rows.note: The note relates the early-position allocation to the greater spread of the ground-truth positional embeddings at early positions.
rows.check: For V4 the row is observed: all positions are covered. For V5 it is partial: about 50 features span ranges of positions rather than one per position. The authors suggest the count depends on SAE width, which bears on whether these units are canonical.

source_check.correct: V4: observed; all positions receive positional features. V5: cannot_determine; features spanning position ranges does not establish incomplete, unstable or noncanonical dictionary units.
source_check.locator_found: Summary; Positional features; Discussion, first paragraph
source_check.problem: The shared partial state understates V4 coverage and treats an untested V5 property as an incomplete effect.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Measured positional feature activations while varying the input token at fixed positions.
rows.measure: Variation in positional feature activation over input tokens
rows.value: Many positional features have small standard deviation over input tokens.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as evidence that these are true positional features.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared the top three PCA components of positional embeddings with learned SAE feature directions.
rows.measure: Variance explained by top three PCA components and recovery of positional-embedding manifold by SAE features
rows.value: Top 3 PCA components explain 95% of the positional embedding matrix variance; SAE features together recover the 1 dimensional helical manifold.
rows.note: The position 0 embedding and SAE features are omitted in the figure caption.
rows.check: Top 3 PCA components explain 95% of positional-embedding variance, and the SAE tiles this helical manifold with many features. That also bears on V6, since the positional variable sits on a multi-dimensional curved manifold. It bears on V5 too: the authors say per-feature explanations lose this geometry.

source_check.correct: V4: observed. V5 and V6: cannot_determine from this measurement. The top three PCs explain 95% of variance for positional-embedding rows 1–127; the authors describe a one-dimensional helical manifold recovered collectively by many SAE features.
source_check.locator_found: Summary, Figure 1 caption; Discussion, feature geometry paragraph
source_check.problem: PCA variance and manifold coverage do not establish canonical dictionary units or irreducibly multidimensional superposed features.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Held token or position fixed and varied the other input to compare feature activations.
rows.measure: Separation of positional and semantic feature activations
rows.value: Positional and semantic features are described as (almost) entirely disjoint at layer 0.
rows.note: The authors say this should not be expected to continue in later layers, where attention mixes semantic and positional information.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Averaged feature activations over positions to inspect token-associated features.
rows.measure: Feature activation patterns for a fixed token
rows.value: For a fixed token, the note generally finds strong or weak token-dependent features and lower-magnitude position-dependent features that activate conditionally on sequence position.
rows.note: The post says these patterns are illustrated for particular tokens.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Extended positional feature activation plots to positions beyond the SAE training context.
rows.measure: Positional feature activation and positional interpretation outside the training context
rows.value: Positional features overfit to short contexts; at late positions the SAE appears to interpret positions as significantly earlier positions.
rows.locator: Length generalization of SAEs; Positional features break
rows.note: The post describes the feature behavior as becoming unusual beyond the SAE context length.
rows.check: Out-of-context breakage is a property of the SAE, not of the model's features, so V4 does not apply. Stability of the positional features is absent beyond position 128. 'Partial' understates this: the authors call it 'pretty fundamentally broken'.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected token-associated semantic feature activations across positions.

conditions.value: within SAE context length, through position 127

rows.measure: Stability of semantic feature activations across positions
rows.value: Features that fire for given tokens have stable activations until the end of the SAE context length.
rows.locator: Length generalization of SAEs; Semantic features break
rows.note: This is a within-training-context observation, not a test across models or SAE trainings.

source_check.correct: V4: observed. V5: cannot_determine; token-associated activations remain stable across positions within the training context, but dictionary completeness and canonicality are not measured.
source_check.locator_found: Length generalization of SAEs, Semantic features break
source_check.problem: Activation stability across positions is insufficient to establish V5's complete, stable, canonical units.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected semantic feature activations for positions beyond the SAE training context.
rows.measure: Noise and spurious activation in semantic features
rows.value: Semantic feature activations become noisier; features that did not fire at small positions can start firing. An arrow-associated feature also fires on the word “leep” late in the context.
rows.locator: Length generalization of SAEs; Semantic features break
rows.note: The post presents the arrow-feature example as a false indication that arrows are present.
rows.check: This concerns SAE behaviour beyond its training context, not whether the model contains recoverable features, so V4 is removed. Semantic features become noisy or fire falsely, for example an arrow feature firing on 'leep'. Stability is absent in that regime.

relationships.reason: The SAE recovers about 50 token-invariant positional features covering all positions and tiling the positional manifold. It also recovers semantic features, almost disjoint from the positional ones (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6).
relationships.display_finding: The SAE recovered about 50 token-invariant positional features that covered all positions and tiled the positional manifold, plus semantic features almost disjoint from them.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R1–R6 document recovered positional and semantic features, including approximately 50 positional features spanning the training context.

relationships.condition: gpt2-small layer 0 SAE, within training context
relationships.reason: A continuous positional manifold is split into about 50 range-covering features, and the authors say per-feature explanations miss its geometry (R2, R4). Semantic features are stable within context (R8).
relationships.display_finding: A continuous positional manifold was split into about 50 range-covering features whose individual explanations miss its geometry, while semantic features stayed stable within the training context.

source_check.condition: gpt2-small layer 0 SAE, within training context
source_check.reason: R2, R4 and R8 show positional ranges, collective geometry and within-context activation stability. They do not test completeness or canonicality; V5 does not require one feature per position.

relationships.condition: gpt2-small layer 0 SAE, positions beyond SAE context length 128
relationships.reason: Positional features mislocalize, and semantic features become noisy or fire spuriously (R7, R9). The units therefore depend on the SAE's training distribution, not only on the model.
relationships.display_finding: Positional features mislocalized and semantic features became noisy or fired spuriously, so the units depended on the SAE's training distribution and not only on the model.

relationships.reason: Position lies on a helical manifold in about 3 dimensions (95% of variance), which the SAE represents with many 1-D features (R4). This suggests a multi-dimensional feature being chopped into directions.
relationships.display_finding: Position lies on a helical manifold occupying about 3 dimensions (95% of variance), which the SAE represents with many 1-D features, suggesting a multi-dimensional feature chopped into directions.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R4 concerns a manifold explicitly described as one-dimensional. Its curved embedding and variance across three PCs do not establish irreducibly multidimensional features being superposed.

statements.problem: The positional-study facts are correct, but their placement as limits_scope evidence against V6 conflates curved geometry with multidimensional superposed features.
